title: Coin Flip: A Small Browser Game With Shared Results
author: Jason Lamb
excerpt: A responsive coin flip with independent random outcomes, accessible controls, reduced motion, and a shared results history.

cover.alt: Illustrated gold smiling coin spinning above a dark background with a cross on the reverse

content_html:
Coin Flip turns a quick decision into a small interactive browser experience. A flip starts when the page loads; visitors can flip again by tapping the coin, pressing the button, or using the keyboard. Heads appears as a smiling face and tails as a cross.

The browser chooses each outcome with a cryptographic random bit. Every flip is independent, so a run of heads does not make tails more likely next time. The animation, confetti, and result display make the choice visible, while the page still gives an immediate result when reduced motion is preferred.

A shared history panel shows lifetime totals, percentages, and the 50 most recent outcomes. The server records results separately from the public display. Its private log includes visitor network and browser metadata, which the public history endpoint does not return. If the history service is unavailable, the coin can still flip and reports that the result was not saved.

The project is deliberately small, but its details matter: keyboard controls, focus handling, rapid-click protection, mobile layout, and a clear boundary between public statistics and private log data.
